FLAG: HTB{unp4ck3d_th3_s3cr3t_0f_th3_p455w0rd}

HOW IT WAS RECOVERED
1. Identification: /workspace/packed (8848 bytes) is a UPX 4.22 packed ELF (md5 fe8582ceaf207502a09ce86997ed9d6a); `strings` on it yields zero literal "HTB", and repacking the decompressed image reproduces `packed` byte-identically (cmp rc=0), proving the extraction is faithful. `upx -d packed -o unpacked` gives a 17792-byte, not-stripped GTK4 x86-64 PIE ELF.
2. Code path: main @0x175f -> activate @0x1508 builds the GTK window; the "changed" signal handler `entered()` @0x1339 does: buffer text -> strstr(text, "HTB{" /* .rodata 0x2050 */) -> strchr(p,'}') (missing '}' -> tag "black") -> strncmp(p, 0x2060, 7) -> apply tag "green" if equal, else "red". There is no argv/stdin/file/network input path and no flag printing; verification is only the green/red tag. Note the compare length is 7, so static control flow alone only proves "HTB{unp"; the full string comes from the referenced .rodata literal and was confirmed at runtime.
3. Recovery of the full literal: .rodata at 0x2060 holds HTB{unp4ck3d_th3_s3cr3t_0f_th3_p455w0rd}. Verified three ways — (a) direct byte dump `dd if=unpacked bs=1 skip=0x2060 count=40 | od -c` reproduces exactly that string (inner length 35, matching the 35-asterisk mask); (b) gdb breakpoint filtered to strncmp n==7 shows arg2 = PIE base+0x2060 = "HTB{unp4ck3d_th3_s3cr3t_0f_th3_p455w0rd}"; (c) an LD_PRELOAD strncmp hook logs arg2's raw bytes 48 54 42 7b ... 64 7d = the same string, and driving the program with it via a GTK4 stub yields tag "green" while a wrong flag yields "red".
4. Decoys ruled out (must NOT be reported): 0x2008 "Hr3t_0f_th3_p45}" (lea'd into a dead stack slot, never read) and 0x2019 "HTB{unp4ck3dr3t_HH0f_th3_pH0f_th3_pH0f_th3_pH0f_th3_pH" (54 inner chars, unclosed, no code xrefs). The apparent "second HTB{ at image+0x3050" seen under gdb is not new data: the RW PT_LOAD (off 0x2da0/vaddr 0x3da0) is page-aligned down to off 0x2000 -> vaddr 0x3000, so the .rodata page is mapped twice (0x2050 appears again at 0x3050). A whole-file scan finds exactly three HTB sites: 0x2019, 0x2050, 0x2060.

CAVEATS / CONDITIONS
- libgtk-4.so.1 is absent in the container, so the original binary cannot run natively; runtime confirmation used a local stub GTK4 plus an LD_PRELOAD strncmp hook, and static analysis. The flag does not depend on those shims: it is the literal the program's own strncmp targets.
- Static-only reading of the 7-byte compare would justify only "HTB{unp"; the full 39-character value rests on the .rodata literal at 0x2060 plus the runtime argument dumps agreeing on it.
- Both delegated workstreams (Agent 57 static, Agent 58 dynamic) completed and agree; no paused or unfinished Agents remain.
